title: Secrets Manager + RDS
scenario: Store database credentials in Secrets Manager and make sure the database is encrypted and private.
constraints: Instance is encrypted and not public.

focus.title: Complete the aws_db_instance resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_db_instance.

hints.why: Secrets should live in a managed secret store, not in code or state. Rotation and access policy are easier to audit there.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_db_instance" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_db_instance. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use a secret store for credentials and API keys that applications read at runtime.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_db_instance" "this"`. Use this code shape: identifier; engine; engine_version; instance_class; allocated_storage; skip_final_snapshot; storage_encrypted; publicly_accessible; tags. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `aws_secretsmanager_secret.this.arn`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
